q: Where do you add MCP server JSON for Copilot cloud agent at repository level?
o: A file named mcp.txt in the repo root
e: The repo-level MCP configuration is entered in repository settings.

q: An MCP server needs an API key. How should it be supplied?
o: As an Agents secret named with the COPILOT_MCP_ prefix, referenced from env
e: Only COPILOT_MCP_-prefixed Agents secrets/variables are available to the MCP config.

q: Which `tools` setting best follows least privilege for a third-party MCP server?
o: An explicit list of specific read-only tools
e: Copilot uses MCP tools without asking approval, so allowlist only what is needed.

q: Which `type` values does cloud agent accept for MCP servers?
e: The documented values are local, stdio, http and sse.

q: Select TWO limitations of MCP support in Copilot cloud agent and code review.
o: Only MCP tools are supported, not resources or prompts
Remote servers that use OAuth are not supported
Only one MCP server may be configured
e: Tools only, and no OAuth-based remote servers.

q: Which MCP servers are enabled by default for cloud agent?
e: The GitHub and Playwright MCP servers are on by default.

q: The default GitHub MCP server token can do what?
o: Read-only access to the current repository
Write to all repos in the org
e: It is a specially scoped read-only token for the current repository.

q: Which remote GitHub MCP URL provides the read-only variant?
e: The documented read-only endpoint is /mcp/readonly.

q: Which header selects which toolsets the remote GitHub MCP server exposes?
e: X-MCP-Toolsets lists toolsets such as repos,issues,pull_requests.

q: How do you confirm your MCP servers actually started for a cloud agent run?
o: Check the 'Start MCP Servers' step in the session log
Look at the repo's star count
e: The session log's Start MCP Servers step lists started servers and their tools.

q: Your MCP server needs `uv`, which is not on the default runner. What is the right fix?
o: Ask the agent to download it at random times
e: Setup steps prepare the agent's environment before it starts.

q: What file and job name configure the cloud agent environment?
e: The workflow must contain a job named copilot-setup-steps.

q: The agent cannot reach a package host because of the firewall. Best response?
o: Add the specific host to the custom allowlist
Give the agent an org-admin token
e: Allowlist only what is required; keep the firewall on.

q: Which branch can cloud agent push to when started from an issue?
e: It can push to one branch; branch protections and required checks still apply.

q: Which action can cloud agent NOT perform?
o: Approve and merge its own PR
Push commits to its copilot/ branch
e: It cannot mark Ready for review, approve or merge.

q: By default, when do Actions workflows run on an agent's PR?
o: After a user with write access clicks Approve and run workflows
e: Workflow runs wait for human approval by default (configurable).

q: A tool call fails intermittently with HTTP 503. Best handling?
o: Bounded retries with backoff, then escalate
e: Transient errors justify limited retries; unbounded retries hide problems and burn cost.

q: A tool call is rejected because the tool is not on the allowlist. What now?
o: Do not retry; fix permissions deliberately or escalate to a human
e: Deterministic denials do not self-heal; change permissions only through a reviewed decision.

q: The agent's PR contains a bad change. What is the cleanest rollback before merge?
o: Close the draft PR or revert commits on the copilot/ branch
e: Branch isolation means main is unaffected; discard or revert the branch work.

q: Which of these provides traceability for a cloud agent commit?
o: Commit authored by Copilot, requester as co-author, signed, message links the session log
An unsigned commit with no link
A commit authored by the admin
A commit squashed to hide authorship
e: These attributes support accountability and auditing.

q: An enterprise wants only vetted MCP servers to be usable by Copilot. What should an admin use?
o: An MCP allowlist and/or registry policy
e: Allowlist and registry controls govern which MCP servers are permitted. Verify exact policy names in docs.
